newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, rising trend to resume.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, rising trend to resume.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Thursday with marginal losses among some of the blue chips, but traders expected a rising trend to resume due to solid buying interest.
They predicted a steady growth for Zagrebacka Banka, as there was an increased demand for its shares.
"But (drugs firm) Pliva could edge down very soon," Ivan Hren of Ceufin brokers said, adding he did not expect much trading with Pliva's shares for a week or two.
He also said elections in neighbouring Bosnia could have a slight influence on price movements in Zagreb.
"If the elections go well, we can expect fresh interest of foreign investors," he said.
* Three of seven active issues rose, three fell and one was flat.
* Hotelier Laguna climbed 18 kuna to 818, trading 9 shares.
* Confectioner Kras added five kuna to a new high of 320 on volume of 15 shares.
* Hotelier Jadranturist rose five kuna to 165, with 183 shares sold.
* Pliva remained stable at 12,000 kuna on volume of 89 shares.
* Most actively traded Zagrebacka lost five kuna to close at 735, with 2,688 shares changing hands.
* Food processor Podravka edged down 10 kuna to 225, selling 100 shares.
* Hotelier Istraturist lost 20 kuna to close at 140, with 100 shares sold.
* Daily volume down at 3,184 shares, turnover slightly lower at 3.1 million kuna.
